items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: WPA bands were bands that the government had sponsored, when President Roosevelt was bringing the nation out of the Depression.

ctx.x: Detroit was really a sporting town, you know. Everything was going. All kind of hustles were going on. Whatever your game was, it was working, you know. And the numbers were very, very big then, you know, where you put so much on a number and then the number comes out that day, and if you catch it, you win. And there were good odds, 500-to-1. And the numbers man had a lot of money, and they'd be sportin' it up, or just livin' it up... It was really good times. Even though times were a little hard, it was still…
